import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Conjecture 8.59

by V. M. Poletskikh, I. V. Protasov

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/

namespace Kourovka.«8.59»

/--
Suppose that $G$ is a locally compact Hausdorff topological group which is locally
nilpotent, meaning that every finitely generated subgroup of $G$ is nilpotent, and
that every proper closed normal subgroup of $G$ is compact. Does $G$ contain a
subgroup which is simultaneously open, compact, and normal?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20 22]
theorem kourovka.«8.59» : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∀ (G : Type) [Group G] [TopologicalSpace G] [IsTopologicalGroup G]
      [T2Space G] [LocallyCompactSpace G],
      (∀ H : Subgroup G, H.FG → Group.IsNilpotent H) →
      (∀ N : Subgroup G, N ≠ ⊤ → IsClosed (N : Set G) → N.Normal →
        IsCompact (N : Set G)) →
      ∃ K : Subgroup G, IsOpen (K : Set G) ∧ IsCompact (K : Set G) ∧ K.Normal := by
  sorry

end Kourovka.«8.59»

Expanded “locally nilpotent” directly as `∀ H : Subgroup G, H.FG → Group.IsNilpotent H`, using Mathlib's existing finite-generation and group-nilpotence predicates.
Represented a proper subgroup by `N ≠ ⊤`; imposed closedness, normality, and compactness on its carrier as a subset of `G`.
Did not require the requested open compact normal subgroup to be proper or nontrivial, preserving the stated allowance that it may be trivial or all of `G`.

import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Conjecture 8.59

by V. M. Poletskikh, I. V. Protasov

Suppose that, in a locally compact locally nilpotent group $G$, all proper
closed normal subgroups are compact. Does $G$ contain an open compact normal
subgroup?

Here a group is locally nilpotent if every finitely generated subgroup is
nilpotent, and locally compact groups are Hausdorff.

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/

namespace Kourovka.«8.59»

/-- A group $G$ is locally nilpotent if every finitely generated subgroup of $G$
is nilpotent. -/
def IsLocallyNilpotent (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∀ H : Subgroup G, H.FG → Group.IsNilpotent H

/-- Every nilpotent group is locally nilpotent. -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem IsLocallyNilpotent.of_isNilpotent (G : Type*) [Group G] [Group.IsNilpotent G] :
    IsLocallyNilpotent G :=
  fun _ _ => inferInstance

/--
Suppose that, in a locally compact locally nilpotent group $G$, all proper
closed normal subgroups are compact. Does $G$ contain an open compact normal
subgroup?

Here $G$ is a Hausdorff topological group whose underlying group is locally
nilpotent, "proper" means $N \neq G$, and the subgroup asked for must be
open, compact and normal at the same time.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20 22]
theorem kourovka.«8.59» : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∀ (G : Type) [Group G] [TopologicalSpace G] [IsTopologicalGroup G] [T2Space G]
      [LocallyCompactSpace G], IsLocallyNilpotent G →
      (∀ N : Subgroup G, N.Normal → IsClosed (N : Set G) → N ≠ ⊤ → IsCompact (N : Set G)) →
      ∃ N : Subgroup G, N.Normal ∧ IsOpen (N : Set G) ∧ IsCompact (N : Set G) := by
  sorry

end Kourovka.«8.59»

Suppose that, in a locally compact locally nilpotent group $G$, all proper closed
normal subgroups are compact. Does $G$ contain an open compact normal subgroup?

Here a group is locally nilpotent if every finitely generated subgroup is nilpotent,
and, as usual in topological group theory, locally compact groups are assumed to be
Hausdorff.

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/

namespace Kourovka.«8.59»

/-- A group $G$ is *locally nilpotent* if every finitely generated subgroup of $G$ is
nilpotent. -/
def IsLocallyNilpotent (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∀ H : Subgroup G, H.FG → Group.IsNilpotent H

/-- Every nilpotent group is locally nilpotent. -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem isLocallyNilpotent_of_isNilpotent (G : Type*) [Group G] [Group.IsNilpotent G] :
    IsLocallyNilpotent G :=
  fun _ _ => inferInstance

/-- A finitely generated locally nilpotent group is nilpotent. -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem IsLocallyNilpotent.isNilpotent (G : Type*) [Group G] [Group.FG G]
    (hG : IsLocallyNilpotent G) : Group.IsNilpotent G :=
  Group.isNilpotent_top.mp (hG ⊤ (Group.fg_def.mp ‹_›))

/--
Suppose that, in a locally compact (Hausdorff) locally nilpotent group $G$, all proper
closed normal subgroups are compact. Does $G$ contain an open compact normal subgroup?

Here "proper" means different from $G$ itself; the open compact normal subgroup asked
for is allowed to be trivial or to be all of $G$.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20 22]
theorem kourovka.«8.59» : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∀ (G : Type) [Group G] [TopologicalSpace G] [IsTopologicalGroup G] [T2Space G]
      [LocallyCompactSpace G],
      IsLocallyNilpotent G →
      (∀ N : Subgroup G, N.Normal → N ≠ ⊤ → IsClosed (N : Set G) → IsCompact (N : Set G)) →
      ∃ N : Subgroup G, N.Normal ∧ IsOpen (N : Set G) ∧ IsCompact (N : Set G) := by
  sorry

end Kourovka.«8.59»
attempts.decomposition_objections: None. The single slot matches the statement, and its notes (Hausdorff convention, 'proper' = ≠ G, the subgroup may be trivial or all of G) agree with my reading.
modeling_decisions: 'Locally compact group' is read, per the standard convention in topological group theory (and the decomposition notes), as a Hausdorff locally compact topological group: `[IsTopologicalGroup G] [T2Space G] [LocallyCompactSpace G]`. Dropping `T2Space` would quantify over a strictly larger class of groups.

'Locally nilpotent' is formalized as: every finitely generated subgroup `H` (as `Subgroup.FG`) is nilpotent as a group (`Group.IsNilpotent ↥H`, i.e. its upper central series reaches ⊤ in finitely many steps). This is the standard definition.

'Proper' is `N ≠ ⊤`; the trivial subgroup counts as a proper closed normal subgroup (compact anyway). Closed/open/compact are stated on the carrier set `(N : Set G)`; an open subgroup is automatically closed so no closedness is added to the conclusion.

The asked-for subgroup is only required to be normal, open and compact; it may be `⊥` (discrete G) or `⊤` (compact G), matching the decomposition notes. The trivial group satisfies the hypotheses vacuously and the conclusion via `⊤`.

The bespoke definition `IsLocallyNilpotent` is generic and would normally belong in FormalConjecturesForMathlib/; it is kept in the problem file only because the task restricts all output to the single candidate file (same pattern as Kourovka/1_40.lean, which keeps `IsEngelGroup` in the problem file).
The group type is quantified in universe `Type`, matching the other Kourovka files.

import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Conjecture 8.59

by V. M. Poletskikh, I. V. Protasov

Suppose that, in a locally compact locally nilpotent group $G$, all proper closed normal
subgroups are compact. Does $G$ contain an open compact normal subgroup?

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/

namespace Kourovka.«8.59»

/--
Suppose that $G$ is a locally compact Hausdorff topological group such that every finitely
generated subgroup is nilpotent and every proper closed normal subgroup is compact. Does $G$
contain a subgroup that is simultaneously open, compact, and normal?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20 22]
theorem kourovka.«8.59» : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∀ (G : Type) [Group G] [TopologicalSpace G] [IsTopologicalGroup G] [T2Space G]
      [LocallyCompactSpace G],
      (∀ H : Subgroup G, H.FG → Group.IsNilpotent H) →
      (∀ H : Subgroup G, H ≠ ⊤ → IsClosed (H : Set G) → H.Normal →
        IsCompact (H : Set G)) →
      ∃ K : Subgroup G, IsOpen (K : Set G) ∧ IsCompact (K : Set G) ∧ K.Normal := by
  sorry

end Kourovka.«8.59»
modeling_decisions: Interpreted “locally compact group” as a Hausdorff topological group via `T2Space G`, `IsTopologicalGroup G`, and `LocallyCompactSpace G`, as specified by the decomposition notes.
Expressed local nilpotence directly as `∀ H : Subgroup G, H.FG → Group.IsNilpotent H`, matching the stated meaning that every finitely generated subgroup is nilpotent.
Represented a proper closed normal subgroup by `H ≠ ⊤`, `IsClosed (H : Set G)`, and `H.Normal`; represented compactness, openness, and compactness of the witness as properties of its underlying set.
Allowed the requested open compact normal subgroup to be trivial or all of `G`, since the source imposes no properness or nontriviality condition on the witness.
